tasks.title: Audit factor-bearing polynomial degree and divided-derivative consumer
tasks.task:
Work only in /home/mj-kang/Documents/Dev/math/factoring-research. Read AGENTS.md, RESEARCH_TEAM.md, RESEARCH_LOOP.md, README.md, docs/SPECIFICATION.md. No recursive delegation, installs, commits, shared solver/Lean/STATE/task-file edits. Own ONLY research/findings/W029-frobenius-degree-review.md and research/findings/W029-frobenius-degree-review-evidence/. Freeze full brief, load-bearing inputs, hashes and exact read scope. Parent continues independent research.

Audit the complete new parent finding research/findings/W029-frobenius-degree-probe.md, especially its concrete normalized derivative consumer. Define (1+a)^r=F_r(X)+a G_r(X), a²=1−4X; pair powering O(log r) gates. For N=pq distinct odd p<q, F_N=F_q(X^p) modp and F_p(X^q) modq. Claimed exact degrees (N−p)/2 and (N−q)/2 from leading coefficient of F_q=q(-4)^((q−1)/2), so highest nonzero coefficient index r gives p=N−2r and its gcd gives q. Support bound O(p+q); this is NOT actual support lower bound. Values in Fp alias F_q(X^p) with F_q(X), ordinary derivative zero modN. Generic full sparse interpolation is rejected, not a new lower bound.

Actual new computation: over Z[X], F_r'=-2r G_(r−1), hence normalize by r BEFORE reduction: H_N=F_N'/N=-2G_(N−1), computable O(logN) scalar ring operations without divisionbyN. For p|N, x nonzero, A=1−4x nonzero, u=1+a,v=1−a,t=u/v, chi=(A|p). t lives in split group p−1 or norm-one group p+1. H_N(x)=0 iff t^(N−1)=1 iff t^(q−chi)=1. Candidate gcd thus returns to an order condition; subgroup size gcd(N−1,p−chi) is NOT its x-sampling probability. No general split bound and no coefficient extraction. Check signs, degree/support statements, component function aliasing scope, exceptions and real cost. Is there a genuinely different cheap scalar invariant left in this normalization, or is that displayed consumer fully accounted by existing Lucas/order tests? Give exact corrections rather than speculative quotas.

Dedup: W021 section C already proposed Frobenius support/folding; W029 is not a claim to invent it. W028 parity audit just completed separately; do NOT repeat it. W001 algebra/dynamics and W005/W019 contain broad torus/rank/order themes; targeted search is enough. Primary prior art leads: Bluher https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06877 (parent read abstract only, not theorem text), Dickson F_r=D_r(2,4X)/2 likely useful. A recent search returned https://www.mdpi.com/2227-7390/14/13/2378 'On the Factorizations of Integers via Division Algorithms for Polynomials' but fetch429; no claims adopted from it. Check narrowly if directly relevant. Prefer symbolic proof/counterexample. No experiment requested; if a named ambiguity truly needs a small certificate, freeze one <=60sec/20000 events before run, retain all failures, no sweeps/repeats. No factoring bound or novelty claim. Verified complete improvement NONE.
tasks.latestTerminalSummary:
The review is done. Sections 1–3 of W029 are correct with a few wording fixes. The §4 normalized-derivative consumer adds nothing new: existing Lucas and Williams p±1 tests already cover it. Verified improvement: **NONE**.

The review is `research/findings/W029-frobenius-degree-review.md`, with evidence in `research/findings/W029-frobenius-degree-review-evidence/`.

**What holds up:**
- The derivative identity F_r′ = −2r·G_{r−1} is right, and so is the Dickson form 2F_r = D_r(2,4X), G_r = U_r(2,4X).
- The Frobenius reduction, the degrees (N−p)/2 and (N−q)/2, the leading coefficient q(−4)^((q−1)/2), the top-index gcd giving q, and N−2r = p are all correct. The degree claims only hold for N = pq. If p^k exactly divides N, the degree mod p is (N−p^k)/2.
- The order condition t^(q−χ) = 1 is correct. The subgroup size simplifies to gcd(p−χ, q−χ). At the excluded points x ≡ 0 and 1−4x ≡ 0, H_N is nonzero mod p.

**Main correction:** for any x coprime to N, H_N(x) = (F_N(x) − G_N(x))/(2x) mod N. So H_N is just a value of the same circuit's second output, equal to −2·U_{N−1}(2,4x). It is subject to the same aliasing as §2. This is the Lucas analogue of the Fermat gcd, i.e. Williams p±1 with exponent N−1. W001-algebra Card D already covers the N+1 version, and W029 should cite it.

**Exact count instead of "no bound":** let g₊ = gcd(p−1, q−1) and g₋ = gcd(p+1, q+1).
- The number of x in F_p with H_N(x) ≡ 0 is Z = (g₊ + g₋)/2 − 2. The same Z holds over F_q.
- That gives an exact split probability of (Z/p)(1−Z/q) + (Z/q)(1−Z/p).
- When g₊ = g₋ = 2, Z = 0 and the test never splits. N = 35 is an example, and N = 5q with any prime q ≡ 7 (mod 12) gives infinitely many more.

**No other cheap invariant is left.**
- Every higher normalized derivative is a fixed function of x times the single value u^N = (1+a)^N.
- The same is true of normalized Hasse derivatives of order below the smallest prime. This follows from a formal-logarithm identity.
- The first Hasse derivative that is nonzero mod p has order exactly p. Reaching it costs order-p work per gate, about the same as trial division.
- Evaluating in extension rings doesn't escape the aliasing either: it becomes the standard Frobenius twist already covered in the W021 C review.

**Prior art:** the Bluher arXiv page is about Dickson permutation properties, not integer factoring. I read only the abstract and relied on nothing from it. The MDPI link returned 403, so nothing was adopted from it.

**Certificate:** the symbolic argument was enough, but the brief allowed one small run to settle the zero-count question. I froze it before running and ran it once: 4,634 events, about 0.001 s. All five checks matched the predictions. These are toy-input identity checks, not complexity evidence.

The review lists five exact text corrections for the W029 finding. I made no commits and did not touch shared files or W028.
